where: Section 1, formula, worked example 1 (steps 5 and 6), exam trap 4
problem: P1dB,out is redefined as the straight-line (extrapolated) output at the compression input. In datasheets and standard texts the output 1 dB compression point is the measured output, which is already 1 dB below the straight-line value. So the formula P1dB,in = P1dB,out − G and the trap 'P1dB,in and P1dB,out differ by G' are off by 1 dB against every real datasheet a student will read.
fix: Keep the standard meaning: P1dB,out is the measured output at P1dB,in, i.e. P1dB,out = P1dB,in + G − 1 dB, and the straight-line output at that input is P1dB,in + G = P1dB,out + 1 dB. With G = 20 dB and the measured 19 dBm at compression: P1dB,out = 19 dBm, straight-line output = 20 dBm, P1dB,in = 0 dBm. Rewrite the formula as P1dB,in = P1dB,out + 1 dB − G, and change trap 4 to 'the straight-line output at P1dB,in is 1 dB above P1dB,out'.

problem: 'The a3 term makes the gain fall as the signal amplitude rises' is not true for any a3. Compression needs a3 negative; a positive a3 gives gain expansion at low drive.
fix: State the small-signal gain with a cubic term: gain = a1 + (3/4)a3A², where A is the input amplitude in volts. Gain falls only when a3 < 0; that is the compression case used here. (The a2 term creates second-order products and a DC shift.)

problem: The text says the IM3 output is set equal to the output-referred noise floor N + G, but the written equation is 3Pin − 2IIP3 = N, which drops G without showing it cancels.
fix: Write it in one more line: OIM3 = 3Pin − 2IIP3 + G equals N + G, so G cancels and 3Pin − 2IIP3 = N, giving Pin = (2IIP3 + N)/3 and SFDR = Pin − N = (2/3)(IIP3 − N).

problem: The aria text says input and output intercept values are marked, but the plot has only the ideal line and the measured points; no IIP3 or OIP3 marker exists.
fix: Either add markers at (0 dBm, 19/20 dBm) for the 1 dB point and the extrapolated crossing at 10 dBm input / 30 dBm output, or delete the intercept clause from the aria description.

problem: 'A lower IM3 number in dBc means cleaner performance' is ambiguous, because IM3 in dBc is normally a negative number (−40 dBc is cleaner than −30 dBc, yet −40 is the lower number).
fix: Say 'a more negative IM3 level in dBc means cleaner performance; −40 dBc is 10 dB cleaner than −30 dBc'.
